# Overview

Two bar plots: GC% and GC3% of each **part** on its own - the 1xFLAG tag and
each recoded eGFP copy - rather than of the assembled constructs. Every other
notebook in this folder reports whole constructs, where the fixed SmBiT/P2A
backbone and the linkers are mixed in. This is the per-part view, which is what
goes into a synthesis order.

Each part is shown **before and after recoding**, against the MDA-MB-231
expressed median as a reference line, because the single number by itself does
not say whether it is on target.

Both are read from already-exported tables; nothing is recomputed from the
genome, so this notebook is fast.

# 1. Load Libraries

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(Biostrings)

source(here("code", "cds_reporter_design", "reporter_helpers.R"))

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 5)

indir <- here("output", "cds_reporter_design")
```

# 2. The Recoded Parts

```{r read_recoded}
parts_csv <- file.path(indir,
               paste0("08_recoded_parts_", params$run_tag, ".csv"))
stopifnot("Recoded parts table not found: knit 08_ first" =
            file.exists(parts_csv))

rec <- read_csv(parts_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(part = str_remove(part, ",\\s*recoded$"))
stopifnot(
  "Recoded parts table is missing expected columns" =
    all(c("part", "nt", "gc_pct", "gc3_pct") %in% names(rec)),
  "Expected one FLAG part and at least one eGFP copy" =
    sum(rec$part == "FLAG (1x)") == 1 && sum(str_detect(rec$part, "^eGFP")) >= 1
)
print(rec %>% dplyr::select(-cds) %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>% as.data.frame())
```

# 3. The Same Parts Before Recoding

The originals come from the parts spreadsheet, so this notebook does not depend
on `08_` having exported them. Every eGFP copy starts from the same native
sequence, so the three "original" eGFP bars are by definition the same number -
the copies only diverge once they are recoded.

```{r read_originals}
parts_xlsx <- here("accessories", "cds seq.xlsx")
stopifnot("accessories/cds seq.xlsx not found" = file.exists(parts_xlsx))

ptb <- read_excel(parts_xlsx)
names(ptb)[1] <- "construct"
pseq <- ptb %>%
  filter(!is.na(construct), !is.na(cds)) %>%
  transmute(part = tolower(str_trim(construct)),
            seq  = toupper(gsub("\\s", "", cds)))
pseq <- setNames(pseq$seq, pseq$part)

egfp   <- pseq[["egfp"]]
flag1x <- substr(pseq[["flag3x"]], 43, 66)
stopifnot(
  "1xFLAG does not encode the DYKDDDDK epitope" =
    as.character(translate(DNAString(flag1x))) == "DYKDDDDK",
  "egfp is not 723 nt" = nchar(egfp) == 723
)

orig_of <- function(p) if (p == "FLAG (1x)") flag1x else egfp
orig <- rec %>%
  transmute(part,
            nt      = map_int(part, ~ nchar(orig_of(.x))),
            gc_pct  = map_dbl(part, ~ gc_pct_of(orig_of(.x))),
            gc3_pct = map_dbl(part, ~ compute_gc3_pct(orig_of(.x))))

stopifnot(
  "Recoding changed a part's length" = all(orig$nt == rec$nt),
  "Original and recoded GC3 are identical: nothing was recoded" =
    !isTRUE(all.equal(orig$gc3_pct, rec$gc3_pct))
)
print(orig %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
        as.data.frame())
```

# 4. The Background Reference

```{r read_background}
med_csv <- file.path(indir, "01_group_medians_cds_gc.csv")
stopifnot("Background medians not found: knit 01_ first" = file.exists(med_csv))

meds <- read_csv(med_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(group == "All expressed mRNAs")
stopifnot("Expected exactly one 'All expressed mRNAs' row" = nrow(meds) == 1)

BG_GC  <- meds$median_gc_pct
BG_GC3 <- meds$median_gc3_pct
cat("MDA-MB-231 expressed median - GC:", BG_GC, "% | GC3:", BG_GC3,
    "% (n =", format(meds$n, big.mark = ","), ")\n")
```

# 5. The Plots

```{r assemble}
bar_tbl <- bind_rows(orig %>% mutate(version = "Original"),
                     rec  %>% dplyr::select(part, nt, gc_pct, gc3_pct) %>%
                       mutate(version = "Recoded")) %>%
  mutate(part    = factor(part, levels = rec$part),
         version = factor(version, levels = c("Original", "Recoded")))

ver_cols <- c("Original" = "grey70", "Recoded" = "#0072B2")

bar_plot <- function(yvar, bg, ylab, title, caption) {
  ggplot(bar_tbl, aes(part, .data[[yvar]], fill = version)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.78), width = 0.72) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = bg, linetype = 2, color = "grey25") +
    annotate("text", x = 0.55, y = bg, vjust = -0.6, hjust = 0, size = 3.1,
             color = "grey25",
             label = paste0("MDA-MB-231 expressed median, ",
                            round(bg, 1), "%")) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", .data[[yvar]])),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.78),
              vjust = -0.45, size = 3.1, color = "grey20") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = ver_cols, name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab, title = title, caption = caption) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
}
```

## GC content

```{r plot_gc}
p_gc <- bar_plot(
  "gc_pct", BG_GC, "GC (%)",
  "GC content of each part, before and after recoding",
  paste("Parts on their own, not the assembled constructs: the fixed",
        "SmBiT/P2A backbone\nand the linkers are excluded."))
print(p_gc)
ggsave(here("plots", paste0("cds_reporter_11_part_gc_", params$run_tag, ".pdf")),
       p_gc, width = 7.5, height = 5)
```

## GC3

```{r plot_gc3}
p_gc3 <- bar_plot(
  "gc3_pct", BG_GC3, "GC3 (%)",
  "GC3 of each part, before and after recoding",
  paste("FLAG reaches 0% by constraint, not by choice: its five Asp and one",
        "Tyr can only end\nC or T, and its two Lys only A or G, so pulling GC3",
        "down forces every codon to A or T."))
print(p_gc3)
ggsave(here("plots", paste0("cds_reporter_11_part_gc3_", params$run_tag, ".pdf")),
       p_gc3, width = 7.5, height = 5)
```

# 6. What the Two Panels Say

```{r summary}
summ <- bar_tbl %>%
  dplyr::select(part, version, gc_pct, gc3_pct) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(gc_pct, gc3_pct), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = version, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(metric = recode(metric, gc_pct = "GC", gc3_pct = "GC3"),
         target = if_else(metric == "GC", BG_GC, BG_GC3),
         delta  = Recoded - Original,
         miss   = Recoded - target) %>%
  arrange(metric, part)
print(summ %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
        as.data.frame())
```

**The three eGFP copies are indistinguishable on GC3 and nearly so on GC.** All
three land on exactly the same GC3, because the recoder is given a third-base
*count* per block and the copies all get the same count; they differ in which
codons realise it, not in how many. The small GC difference on copy 3 is first-
and second-base divergence in the Leu, Arg and Ser positions, which is the
composition-level trace of the fact that the copies are not a tandem repeat.

**FLAG is not on target and cannot be.** Eight codons is far too few to pull
anything onto a transcriptome median, and the epitope's own composition sets a
hard floor: with GC3 driven down, Asp and Tyr can only end C or T and Lys only
A or G, so GC3 goes to 0%. That is why the bare SmBiT-P2A-FLAG rung sits off
the background on A/T balance while still matching on GC3 once the fixed
backbone is included. An 8-codon acidic tag at GC3 = 0% is not a translation
problem: 51% of expressed MDA-MB-231 transcripts carry a run of 8 consecutive
GC3 = 0% codons, with no difference in riboseq TPM (see the README).

```{r checks}
# The recoding must move eGFP toward the background on GC3 and must not have
# moved it past the target by more than it started away from it.
egfp_rows <- summ %>% filter(metric == "GC3", str_detect(part, "^eGFP"))
stopifnot(
  "Recoding did not lower eGFP GC3" = all(egfp_rows$delta < 0),
  "Recoded eGFP GC3 is further from the target than the original was" =
    all(abs(egfp_rows$miss) < abs(egfp_rows$Original - egfp_rows$target))
)
cat("eGFP GC3 moved", round(mean(egfp_rows$Original), 1), "% ->",
    round(mean(egfp_rows$Recoded), 1), "% against a target of",
    round(BG_GC3, 1), "%\n")

# FLAG is expected to MISS, and saying so is the point. Assert the direction
# rather than the magnitude, so this does not become a check that passes by
# accident if the epitope changes.
flag_gc3 <- summ %>% filter(metric == "GC3", part == "FLAG (1x)")
stopifnot("FLAG GC3 is not at the floor its amino acids impose" =
            flag_gc3$Recoded == 0)
cat("FLAG GC3:", flag_gc3$Original, "% ->", flag_gc3$Recoded,
    "% (floor imposed by DYKDDDDK, not a target)\n")
```

          paste0("11_part_composition_", params$run_tag, ".csv")))
cat("Exported 11_part_composition_", params$run_tag, ".csv\n", sep = "")
